message:
As Enclosure and Structural Designer, the grown array still stands on soft soil without sinking, Manager.

In plain words one small car of weight on six feet stays well below soft ground capacity even with three extra modules. Total with grown nine-module allowance is 1840 kg in the grown mass calc (E87), about one small car, giving 18.8 kPa per pad in the grown pad pressure calc (E89) on six 400 mm pads, well below the 150 kPa allowable in Structural Design Calculation Sheet | PDF | Strength Of Materials | Precast Concrete (E62), so my prior 18.2 kPa check holds with margin.

The separate ground frame for seven modules must be anchored against wind, Solar Energy Systems Engineer.

In plain words seven parking-space sails can lift lighter than their own frames in a storm so they need ground screws not just feet. Nine modules cover 17.6 square metres in the nine-module footprint calc (E84) from module size 1722 by 1134 mm in PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Performance (E64), and 25 metre per second gust gives 375 Pa in the gust pressure calc (E88), which over that area lifts like 673 kg in the uplift calc (E90), heavier than the frame itself, so the ground frame gets four screw anchors plus the roof gantry keeps its vent gap with no loads into sandwich panels. Photovoltaic means PV, solar-electric panel.

I take up the door rule in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) that Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist put on the board, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer.

In plain words his leak maths and my door choice agree. That guide states standard doors are 900 mm wide with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains and self-closing hinges, which passes one 600 by 400 mm crate plus carrier under eight openings discipline for only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day door loss, and I qualify the wall-ceiling plates in Reliable Refrigerated Transport | Cold Car & Delvic Foods (E52) from structures side as 100 to 150 kg on through-bolted rails with sealed rear penetration and outside drain to keep the Polyisocyanurate (PIR, rigid foam insulation) box hose-cleanable.

I am ready, because mass, split footings and door interfaces close with only the 43 degree pull-down bench test left as named hardware test.
